quote: Give me Books, fruit, French wine and fine weather and a little music out of doors, played by somebody I do not know.
source: John Keats, Letters, to Fanny Keats, Winchester, 28 August 1819 (ed. Sidney Colvin, 1891), p. 285

evidence.where: a page scan of Sidney Colvin’s edition, Letters of John Keats to his Family and Friends, where letter CXIII is headed TO FANNY KEATS, Winchester, August 28 [1819] and the sentence stands on p. 285 in exactly this wording, capital Books and capital French included
evidence.locator: letter CXIII, to Fanny Keats, Winchester, 28 August 1819, p. 285

reason: Word for word in Colvin, including the capitals the proposal kept and the word order that the Calendar For Life card had scrambled. The sentence runs on after a dash, so the full stop marks a cut at a complete imperative clause, which changes nothing in the sense.
